paragraphs: Ameru chakamim za"l qana o asa malbushim chadashim mebarek shehecheyanu mippene shehu sameach bahem ulekak mebarek lehashshem yitbarek al asher zikkahu lesimcha zo, vahagam ki mishshurat haddin hu lebarek beet haqqeniyya o haasiyya nahagu haolam lebarek beet shellobesham, ak yesh omerim sheim qana o asa ezeh malbush chadash az keshellobesho mebarek birkat malbish arumim, ubeezor kesheozer bo mebarek ozer yisrael bigbura, vehakkoba keshemmesimo berosho mebarek oter yisrael betipara, veyesh choleqin usebira lehu deen lebarek berakot ellu umishshum sapeq berakot ellu lo nahagu haolam lebarekam, umikkol maqom tob lelabesham paam harishon beshacharit vikavven alehem veyilbasham tekep achar birkot hashshachar belo hessach haddaat vehepseq ubazeh yatza yede chobato lekulle alema, veim hu mukrach lelabesham arbit yomar alehem berakot hannizkarot beli shem umalkut viharher shem umalkut belibbo:

clarification.explanation: One who buys or makes a new garment that gives him joy recites Shehecheyanu, as thanksgiving to Hashem for having merited him this joy. By strict law one should bless at the time of purchase or manufacture, but the custom is to bless at the time of wearing. Some say that when one wears a new garment he also blesses 'malbish arumim,' on a belt 'ozer Yisrael bigvurah,' and on a hat 'oter Yisrael betif'arah'; but some disagree, and because of the doubt the custom is not to recite these. Good advice: wear them for the first time in the morning immediately after the morning blessings without interruption and have them in mind, and thereby fulfill all opinions; and if one is compelled to wear them at night, he should say these blessings without Hashem's Name and Kingship and mentally intend the Name and Kingship in his heart.
takeaways: A new garment that brings joy - one blesses Shehecheyanu (the custom is to do so at the time of wearing).
To also fulfill 'malbish arumim' and the others, wear them for the first time in the morning right after the morning blessings.

paragraphs: Apillu im qana beged shekkebar labash oto adam acher kol shehu sameach bo yebarek shehecheyanu veken hu haddin im natenu lo beged bemattana ap al pi sheeno chadash yebarek alayv meachar shessamach bo:

clarification.explanation: Even if one bought a garment that someone else had already worn, as long as he is joyful in it he blesses Shehecheyanu. And likewise, if he received a garment as a gift, even though it is not new, he blesses over it, since he is joyful in it.
takeaways: The measure is joy: even a used garment or a gift requires Shehecheyanu if it brings joy.

paragraphs: Al chaluq umiknasayim uminal veanniplaot lo yebarek "p shessameach bahem abal chatzi beged sheqqorin bearbe yl"q (apuda seruga chareppit) o mah sheqqorin tzdry"y (apuda mekupteret) im hem chashuben vesamach bahem yebarek:

clarification.explanation: On a shirt, trousers, shoes, and socks one does not bless Shehecheyanu even though he is joyful in them. But on a significant outer garment (such as a winter vest/sweater) that gives him joy, he does bless.
takeaways: Basic/undergarments - no Shehecheyanu.
A significant outer garment that brings joy - one blesses Shehecheyanu.

paragraphs: Im hu ashir veasa beged chadash sheeno chashub etzlo veeno sameach bo lo yebarek "p dezeh habbeged im haya etzel aniyyim haya chashub etzlam usemechim bo zeh hakkelal kol shessameach mebarek abal eno sameach lo yebarek vekol adam qim leh benapsheh ek hu:

clarification.explanation: A wealthy man who made a new garment that is not significant in his eyes and he is not joyful in it does not bless, even though that same garment would be significant and joyful to a poor person. The rule is: whoever is joyful blesses, and whoever is not joyful does not bless; and every person knows within himself how he feels.
takeaways: The blessing depends on personal joy, which varies from person to person.

paragraphs: Qana kelim chadashim shessamach bahem mebarek beshaa shemmishtammesh bahem ak lo nahagu haolam bazeh veayyen mishbetzot zahab sop siman rk"g hattaam vehoil venahagu "p shehattaam qalush lo yebarek ki birkat shehecheyanu teluya bamminhag veim kol zeh yere shamayim yishtammesh bahem techilla belel yom tob vibiem lepanayv beet sheomer shehecheyanu beqiddush vikavven lepateram o yishtammesh bahem beet sheyyesh lo peri chadash lebarek shehecheyanu vikavven gam alehem, veim lo epshar lo behaki sherotzeh lehishtammesh bahem tekep az yebarek beli shem umalkut viharher shem umalkut belibbo:

clarification.explanation: One who buys new vessels that give him joy should, by strict law, bless Shehecheyanu at the time of use, but the custom has not been to bless (and the blessing of Shehecheyanu depends on custom). A God-fearing person should use them for the first time on the night of the festival and bring them before him when he says Shehecheyanu at Kiddush and intend to discharge them thereby, or use them when he has a new fruit before him and intend them as well. And if he is compelled to use them immediately, he should bless without Hashem's Name and Kingship and mentally intend the Name and Kingship in his heart.
takeaways: New vessels - the custom is not to bless over them alone.
It is worthwhile to combine them with the Shehecheyanu of a festival or of a new fruit.

paragraphs: Bana bayit chadash o qana bayit banuy meacherim mebarek shehecheyanu, veatta nahagu sheen mebarekim shehecheyanu al habbayit ella osim lo chinnuk bisuda lehodot laAdonai al hattoba haqqayyemet hazzot veyesh semek lasseuda middibre rabbotenu za"l bammidrash (tanchuma bereshit d) ulekak niqret seuda shel mitzva, venahagu sheyyilbosh baal habbayit beged chadash betok otah seuda vibarek alayv shehecheyanu vikavven al habbayit:

clarification.explanation: One who builds a new house or buys a house that is already built should, by strict law, bless Shehecheyanu, but now the custom is not to bless Shehecheyanu over the house, but rather to make a 'chanukat habayit' feast to give thanks to Hashem for the good. The custom is that the master of the house wears a new garment during that feast and blesses Shehecheyanu over it, intending it also for the house.
takeaways: A new house - one makes a house-dedication feast.
One blesses Shehecheyanu by means of a new garment at the feast, intending it also for the house.

paragraphs: Lav davqa bana bayit shalem dehaynu hechatzer vekol chadarayv vaaliyyotayv, ella apillu bana bechatzer shehaya lo mikkebar chadarim vaaliyyot mechuddashim shehu sameach bahem yaaseh ken liqnot beged chadash lebarek shehecheyanu vikavven al binyan hechadash ak en tzarik laasot chinnuk bisuda:

clarification.explanation: This is not specific to a whole house, but even if one added, to a courtyard he already owned, new rooms or upper stories in which he is joyful, he should buy a new garment and bless Shehecheyanu over it, intending the new construction; but for this there is no need to make a dedication feast.
takeaways: Even a significant addition of construction requires Shehecheyanu (by means of a garment), without a feast.

paragraphs: "p sheameru chakamenu za"l yaleda ishto zakar mebarek hattob vehammetib lo nahagu haolam lebarek beraka zo veraq nahagu shehaab yebarek shehecheyanu bishat hammila, veim lo nimtza haab umalu oto haqqerobim en mebarekim, mihu yesh omerim kesheyyabo abi habben aach"k yebarek shehecheyanu kesheroeh hattinoq deaz sameach biriyyato, veyesh choleqin bazeh laken bemaqom shennahagu lebarek yebareku, ubemaqom sheen minhag yadua ubarur bazeh lo yebareku mishshum deqayma lan sapeq berakot lehaqel ella yishtaddel lebarek al beged chadash o peri chadash beet sheroeh hattinoq vikavven alayv gam ken, ubeet sheddarashti dabar zeh betzibbur nimtza sham mori harab za"l, veheid al ateret rashe harab haggaon mv"r zeqeni rabbenu mosheh chayyim zlh"h sheraa laabi habben echad shehaya beir acheret bishat hammila uba aach"k veamar lo sheyyebarek shehecheyanu kemo shekkatab "erek lechem" vahalakot qetannot udeammayhu, umeedut zo anachnu lemedin deminhag irenu mizzeman qadmon lebarek, deal ken hora harab mor zeqeni zlh"h leoto haish lebarek ap al gab deyada sheyyesh bedabar zeh pelugta:

clarification.explanation: Although the Sages said that one whose wife bore a son blesses 'HaTov VeHaMeitiv,' this has not been the custom; rather, the custom has been that the father blesses Shehecheyanu at the time of the circumcision. If the father is not present and relatives circumcised the child, one does not bless; and some say that when the father comes afterward and sees the infant with joy, he should bless Shehecheyanu. Because of the dispute: in a place where the custom is to bless, they should bless, and where there is no clear custom, they should not bless (a case of doubt regarding blessings is resolved leniently), but rather he should bless over a garment or new fruit at the time he sees the infant and intend it for this as well. And from this testimony the Ben Ish Chai learned that the custom of his city from ancient times has been to bless - and therefore a father who was not present at the circumcision blesses Shehecheyanu when he sees the infant.
takeaways: The birth of a son - the custom is that the father blesses Shehecheyanu at the circumcision.

A father who was not present blesses Shehecheyanu upon seeing the infant, since the custom of our city from ancient times has been to bless; and where there is no clear custom, he should bless over a garment or new fruit and intend it for this as well.

paragraphs: Kesheyyaggia leshishshim o leshibim nakon lilbosh beged chadash o yiqqach peri chadash vibarek alayv shehecheyanu vikavven gam al shenotayv, veyesh osim seuda kesheyyaggiu leshibim, vehamminhag poh irenu y" hammebi seper tora chadash lebet hakkeneset bashshabbat o beyom tob oseh seuda ballayla laohabim vereim, ubeemtza hasseuda yilbash beged chadash vibarek shehecheyanu vikavven al hasseper tora, ubeammud hashshachar molikin hasseper tora lebet hakkeneset beqibbutz qahal rab upizmonim vesimcha gedola vekol hammarbeh hare zeh meshubbach:

clarification.explanation: Upon reaching sixty or seventy, it is proper to wear a new garment or take a new fruit and bless Shehecheyanu, intending it also for one's years; and some make a feast upon reaching seventy. The custom of Baghdad: one who brings a new Torah scroll to the synagogue makes a feast, wears a new garment during it, blesses Shehecheyanu, and intends it for the Torah scroll.
takeaways: Reaching sixty/seventy - one blesses Shehecheyanu (by means of a garment/fruit) intending it for one's years.

paragraphs: Al peri hammitchaddesh mishshana leshana veyesh zeman qabua legiddulo yebarek shehecheyanu, abal perot sheen bahem hekker ben yeshanim lachodashim kegon egozim usheqedim sheqqorin bearbe gv"z (egoz peqan) velu"z (shaqed) vbnd"q (egoz qatan) vpst"q (egoz gan eden, chaleabi) "p shehem mitchaddeshim mishshana leshana veyodea beellu shemmebarek alehem shehem chadashim shel hashshana hahi, apillu hake lo yebarek shehecheyanu meachar sheen begupam hekker ben chadashim lishanim:

clarification.explanation: On a fruit that renews from year to year and has a fixed time for its growth, one blesses Shehecheyanu. But fruits that have no distinguishing feature between old and new, such as walnuts and almonds of various kinds, even though they renew from year to year and even though one knows that these are from the new crop - one does not bless Shehecheyanu over them, because there is no distinguishing feature in their body between new and old.
takeaways: A seasonal fruit with a fixed growing time - Shehecheyanu.
Walnuts and almonds (no distinguishing feature between new and old) - no Shehecheyanu.

paragraphs: Al peri sheqqorin nvm"y (peri hadar qatan, chimmutz) uperi sheqqorin prtq"l (tpv"z) bedin hu shetztzarik lebarek shehecheyanu shehem mitchaddeshim mishshana leshana vegam nikkarim begupam ben chadashim lishanim, ak nahagu poh irenu deen mebarekim alehem shehecheyanu veshamati sheggam beeretz yisrael tvb"b lo nahagu lebarek ubirkat shehecheyanu teluya bamminhag, mihu al etrog heid harab peri haadama shennohagim lebarek alayv shehecheyanu beir haqqodesh yerushalayim tvb"b sheokelim oto belel sheni shel rosh hashshana bimqom peri chadash, upoh irenu y" haetrog hu matoq ak eno matzuy harbeh ki im meat, uminhagenu bebetenu shenneekal etrog qodem yom tob shel chag hassukkot unebarek alayv shehecheyanu, abal qehal adatenu eno matzuy etzlam leakelo qodem sukkot, veraq okelim oto bt"v bishbat shemmebiim limkor vegam otam haqqonim etrog leninua matzniin oto ad t"v bishbat veokelim oto, veellu en tzerikim lebarek shehecheyanu mippene shekkebar bareku shehecheyanu beyom tob rishon shel sukkot bintilat hallulab ubazeh niptar haetrog gam mibbirkat shehecheyanu shel akila ukemo shekkatebu haacharonim za"l, veken haaleti bsh"q mqbtzyl:

clarification.explanation: On certain citrus fruits (such as oranges), by strict law one should bless Shehecheyanu - since they renew from year to year and are distinguishable in their body between new and old - but in Baghdad the custom has been not to bless, and he has also heard that in the Land of Israel they have not become accustomed to blessing (and Shehecheyanu depends on custom). Regarding the etrog, he testified that in Jerusalem the custom is to bless Shehecheyanu when eating it on the second night of Rosh Hashanah as a new fruit; the custom of Rabbi Yosef Chaim's family is to eat an etrog before the festival of Sukkot and bless Shehecheyanu; and one who eats it after having taken it with the lulav does not need Shehecheyanu, since he was already discharged by the Shehecheyanu of the first day of the festival of Sukkot.
takeaways: Certain citrus fruits - the custom has been not to bless Shehecheyanu.
Etrog - customs vary; an etrog taken with the lulav and eaten afterward is exempt from Shehecheyanu.

paragraphs: Al lepet sheqqorin bearbe shlg"m (lepet lebana) veken al peri adama sheqqorin bearbe lhn" (kerub) veken chassa sheqqorin bearbe k"s (chasa) mebarekin shehecheyanu shehem mitchaddeshim mishshana leshana, veqishshuin arukkin sheqqorin bearbe trvz"y (melapepon daq arok) mebarekin shehecheyanu, veen lomar shehem niklalim biklal qishshuin qetzarim sheqqorin kyy"r (melapepon matzuy) ki chaluqin hem beshem ubemareh ubetaam, ak yeraqot shehem kareti vekarpas vegam mah sheqqorin bearbi mdnv"s (ptrvzylyh) en mebarekin mippene shehem gedilim kol hashshana veen zeman qabua lechiddusham:

clarification.explanation: On turnip, cabbage, and lettuce one blesses Shehecheyanu, since they renew from year to year. Also on long cucumbers one blesses, and one should not say that they are included in short cucumbers, because they differ in name, appearance, and taste. But vegetables such as leeks, celery, and parsley - one does not bless, because they grow all year round and there is no fixed time for their renewal.
takeaways: Seasonal vegetables (turnip, cabbage, lettuce, long cucumber) - Shehecheyanu.
Vegetables that grow all year (celery, parsley) - no Shehecheyanu.

paragraphs: Poh ayarenu yesh kamma mine temarim, veyesh shenayim shehem chaluqim zeh mizzeh bemareh ubetaam ubeshem vehem min sheqqorin kstvv"y (tamar bahir qatan vaasisi) umin sheqqorin bgb"n (tamar tzahob bisserani) shehem shechorim veim kol zeh im berak al min sheqqorin kstvv"y lo yebarek shehecheyanu al min sheqqorin bgb"n, mippene sheddaap el pi sheyyesh lahem shem meyuchad kol echad leatzmo, mikkol maqom derek kelal kullam niqraim beshem temarim, amenam yere shamayim yabi lepanayv beet birkat shehecheyanu shelosha minim mah sheqqorin kstvv"y umah sheqqorin bgb"n umah sheqqorin zyd"y (tamar matzuy, keha) vibarek shehecheyanu liptor et kullam veken anachnu nohagim bebittenu mime abotenu vaabot abotenu veyesh poh ayarenu tutim metuqim yotzeim bechodesh iyyar veachar chodesh yotze tutim acherim sheyyesh behahem taam chamitzot veqorim otam bearbe tute dammeseq, vehamminhag lebarek shehecheyanu al zeh vezeh:

clarification.explanation: There are several kinds of dates that differ in appearance, taste, and name, but if one blessed Shehecheyanu over one kind, he does not bless again over another kind, because they are all generally called 'dates.' A God-fearing person brings before him at the time of the blessing three kinds in order to discharge them all. And likewise regarding two kinds of mulberries (sweet ones that come out in Iyar, and afterward sourish mulberries), the custom is to bless Shehecheyanu over this one and that one.
takeaways: Different kinds of the same fruit (dates) - one Shehecheyanu discharges all of them.
One who wishes to be meticulous brings several kinds together at the time of the blessing.

paragraphs: Haokel peri shello nigmar bishshulo deeno mebarek alayv shehecheyanu hinneh im chazar vaakalo achar shennigmar bishshulo yesh omerim yebarek shehecheyanu veyesh omerim deeno mebarek, veim nizdammen leadam dabar kazeh yabi peri chadash acher vibarek alayv veyiptor gam lazeh, o yishma birkat shehecheyanu meadam acher veyitkavvenu shenehem, velaken yesh lehazhir poh irenu bedabar zeh bitmarim sheokelim otam qodem gemar bishshulam veqorin otam bearbe gvz"y (tamre boser) o kl"l tv"sh (terem hahabshala), veken tzarik lehazhiram betappuchim, beram mah shennahagu lebashshel im tabshil besar tappuchim qodem gemar bishshulan en lachush lebirkat shehecheyanu mippene deellu hattappuchim shemmannichim otam betabshil mishtanneh taman harbeh vegam mishtannet qetzat tzuratam, velaken minhag pashut poh irenu lebarek shehecheyanu kesheokelam chayyim achar gemar bishshulam:

clarification.explanation: One who eats a fruit that has not finished ripening does not bless Shehecheyanu over it; and if he ate it again after it finished ripening - some say he blesses and some say he does not bless. In such a case he should bring another new fruit and bless over it, discharging this one as well, or hear Shehecheyanu from another. Therefore one must be careful regarding dates and apples that are eaten before they finish ripening. But apples that are cooked in a meat dish before they finish ripening are of no concern regarding Shehecheyanu (their taste and form change greatly), and the custom is to bless Shehecheyanu when eating them raw after they have ripened.
takeaways: A fruit eaten unripe - whether the blessing applies once it later ripens is disputed; one should discharge it via another new fruit or by hearing the blessing.
Apples cooked in a dish before ripening - no concern regarding Shehecheyanu.

paragraphs: Akal veshakach velo berak shehehecheyanu yesh omerim yebarek al mah sheyyokal aach"k, veyesh omerim deen lebarek meachar shekkebar akal, vesapeq berakot lehaqel velo yebarek ella yishma birkat shehecheyanu meacherim, o yiptor zeh bipri chadash acher veim lo matze lemebad haki yebarek beli shem umalkut viharher shem umalkut belibbo:

clarification.explanation: One who ate and forgot to bless Shehecheyanu - some say he should bless over what he eats afterward, and some say he should not bless since he has already eaten; and in a case of doubt regarding blessings we are lenient - he should not bless, but rather hear Shehecheyanu from others or discharge it via another new fruit; and if this is not possible, he should bless without Hashem's Name and Kingship and mentally intend the Name and Kingship in his heart.
takeaways: Forgetting to bless Shehecheyanu - one does not bless it afterward (a case of doubt); he should hear it from another or discharge it via an additional new fruit.

paragraphs: Katub birushalmi sop pereq asara yuchasin rabbi chizqiyya beshem rab atid adam litten din vecheshbon al kol sheraata enayv velo akal, rabbi elazar chashash lehahi shematata umetzamtzem leh peritin veakil mikkol milla chada beshatta ayyen sham, al ken illu ani shebbeyisrael yishtaddel liqnot mikkol peri chadash leekol mimmennu hu veanshe beto ulebarek shehecheyanu lehodot lah':

clarification.explanation: It is brought in the Jerusalem Talmud that a person is destined to give a reckoning and accounting for everything his eyes saw and he did not eat, and Rabbi Elazar would save small coins and eat from every new thing once a year. Therefore even the poorest of Israel should endeavor to buy from every new fruit and eat from it, he and his household, and bless Shehecheyanu to give thanks to Hashem.
takeaways: It is fitting to eat from every new fruit once a year and bless Shehecheyanu - and even the poor should make the effort to do so.

paragraphs: Hazzakar yitchayyeb bemitzot ben y"g shana veyom echad, al ken bayyom harishon shel shenat y"d yitpos haab et beno beyado veyomar baruk sheppetarani meanesho shel zeh, viharher shem umalkut bilbabo, veyishtaddel laasot seuda laohabim vereim veyazmin bah talmide chakamim veyarbeh bisuda vesimcha keyad Adonai hattoba alayv, shemmisseuda zo yihyeh sanegoreya gedola al yisrael sheyyomru melitze yosher lipne hqb"h ribbono shel olam reeh baneka kamma hem semechim al asher niknasim beol mitzoteka useuda zo niqret seudat mitzva vehabberaka hannizkeret beli shem umalkut veyomar haab otah betok hasseuda vehayyoshebim yebareku et habben sheyyizkeh lattora veyirat shamayim veqiyyum hammitzot, vehaggedolim shebbaqqeruim yannichu yedehem al rosho vibareku oto bebirkat kohanim, veim yodea habben lidrosh bedibre tora yidrosh dabar beitto mah tob, veim lav yidrosh haab, veim lav yidrosh talmid chakam echad ben haqqeruim, vetob dehabben yilbash beged chadash vibarek shehecheyanu vikavven gam al huknesu beoto hayyom beol mitzot, veim en leel yado yebarek al peri chadash, vegam habbat bayyom shettikkanes bechiyyub matztzot "p shello nahagu laasot lah seuda, im kol zeh tihyeh simcha oto hayyom vetilbosh bigde shabbat, veim yesh leel yadah tilbash beged chadash utebarek shehecheyanu utekavven gam al kenisatah beol mitzot, veyesh nohagin laasot bekol shana et yom halleda leyom tob vesiman yapeh hu veken nohagim bebetenu:

Veshamati sheyyesh meqomot nohagim laasot bekol shana seuda bayyom shenniknas bo haadam bibrito shel abraham abinu, uminhag yapeh hu veareb li meod ak lo nahagnu bazeh bebetenu veraq ana abda nahagti lomar bekol shana veshana bayyom shenniknasti bibrito shel abraham abinu baqqasha zo ribbono shel olam galuy veyadua lepaneka ki behayyom hazzeh shehu yom kak lechodesh peloni shehu haya yom shemini leledati, niknasti bibrito shel abraham abinu alayv hashshalom bashshana harishona shennoladti bah, veqiyyem bi abdeka abi mitzvat mila uperia kaasher tzivvita otanu betorateka haqqedosha venitgalla hakkeli hashshelishi shel hayyesod haamitti niqra qodesh qodashim veyatza oro, venitbattela achizat hachitzonim venitchabberu shemona veshibim orot hachasadim, im shemona veshibim orot haggeburot venitmattequ orot haggeburot beorot hachasadim: ana Adonai lemaan shimka haggadol ulemaan rachameka vachasadeka taazreni utesayyeeni lishmor avvat berit qodesh asher chatamta bibsarenu, vetatztzileni mikkol chete umikkol hirhurim raim umachshebot pegumot vetatztzileni mikkol pegam habberit hen bemachshaba hen bedibbur hen bemaaseh hen bechush hareot hen bechush hashshemia hen bishar chushim ubekullam ehyeh tahor biqdushshat habberit beli shum pegam vehirhur ra kelal, utezakkeni sheetgabber al yetzer hara, vetihyeh machashabti qeshura udebuqa biqdushshat tamid, ki berachameka harabbim bacharta banu mikkol haummot veromematnu mikkol halleshonot, vehibdalta otanu mikkol tumotehem vetoabotehem, kakkatub betorateka (vayyiqra y, kv) vaabdil etkem min haammim lihyot li, nodeh leka Adonai elohenu velohe abotenu al shehotzetanu meeretz mitzrayim, upeditanu mibbet abadim veal beriteka shechatamta bibsarenu, veal torateka shellimmadtanu, veal chuqqe retzonak shehodatanu, veal chayyim umazon sheatta zan umeparnes otanu, ana Adonai leb tahor bera li elohim verucha nakon chaddesh beqirbi, vetimshok alay machashabot qedoshot utehorot zekut unekonot, veyihyeh li leb sameach baabodateka tamid, vetaazreni al debar kebod shemeka meatta vead olam amen ken yehi ratzon:

clarification.explanation:
A male becomes obligated in the commandments at thirteen years and one day. On the first day of his fourteenth year, the father takes his son's hand and says, 'Blessed is He who has exempted me from this one's punishment,' mentally intending the Name and Kingship in his heart (without saying it aloud). It is proper that the father endeavor to make a feast for friends and Torah scholars, and increase joy at it greatly - for it is truly a se'udat mitzvah, since it constitutes a great defense for Israel, as the ministering angels say before the Holy One, blessed be He: 'See how joyful Your children are to enter the yoke of Your commandments.' Those present bless the son that he merit Torah, fear of Heaven, and fulfillment of the commandments; the elders among the guests place their hands on his head and bless him with the Priestly Blessing; and if the son can expound words of Torah, he should do so himself, and if not, the father, and if not, one of the Torah scholars among the guests. It is good for the son to wear a new garment and bless Shehecheyanu, intending also his entering into the yoke of the commandments, and if this is not possible, he blesses Shehecheyanu over a new fruit. Also the daughter, on the day she enters into obligation of the commandments - even though the custom has not been to make a feast for her - should nonetheless rejoice that day and wear Shabbat clothing, and if possible wear a new garment and bless Shehecheyanu, intending also her entering into the yoke of the commandments.
Some are accustomed to celebrate the birthday each year as a kind of personal festive day, and this is a good sign. The Ben Ish Chai adds that in other places there is another lovely custom entirely: to make each year a feast on the day a person entered the 'covenant of Abraham our father' - that is, the anniversary of his own circumcision. This custom was not practiced in his house, but he relates that he himself was accustomed to say each year, on the anniversary of his circumcision, a personal petition before Hashem built also on kabbalistic foundations: according to the Kabbalah, on the day of the circumcision itself the 'third vessel of the foundation,' called the 'Holy of Holies,' was revealed and its light went forth, thereby nullifying the grip of the external forces (the sitra achra), and the seventy-eight lights of kindness were joined with the seventy-eight lights of might, thus sweetening the lights of might within the lights of kindness. Against this background, in the petition he mentions the day of his circumcision, asks to preserve the holiness of the covenant of circumcision from any blemish (in thought, speech, and deed), to merit overcoming the evil inclination, and gives thanks to Hashem for having brought Israel out of Egypt and for the covenant, the Torah, and the statutes given to the people of Israel.
takeaways: At age thirteen years and one day, the father says 'Blessed is He who has exempted me from this one's punishment' and holds a se'udat mitzvah, including the guests' blessing and the Priestly Blessing for the son.
The daughter, too, should be made joyful on the day she enters obligation in the commandments and should bless Shehecheyanu, even if the custom has not been to make her a feast.

There is an additional custom to celebrate each year both the day of birth and the anniversary of the circumcision (the covenant of Abraham our father), and to say on that day a personal petition about preserving the holiness of the covenant.

According to the Kabbalah, the day of circumcision is connected to the revelation of the 'foundation' (Holy of Holies) and the joining of the lights of kindness and might - hence the root importance of preserving the holiness of the covenant.
